sources.title: Gauge Fields and Inflation

evidence.text: Background methods include slow-roll analytic solutions, exact power-law ansätze, autonomous dynamical systems and linear stability, and numerical trajectory analysis; multi-vector backgrounds also use tetrad variables.

sources.title: Tensor Bounds on the Hidden Universe

evidence.text: ADM decomposition and lapse/shift constraints in comoving gauge organize interactions. Integrations by parts and appropriate field redefinitions expose ε suppression of ζχχ and mixed ζγχχ vertices, whereas γχχ is unsuppressed by ε.

sources.title: A new mechanism to enhance primordial tensor fluctuations in single field inflation

evidence.text: The long-wavelength solution h_ij = C1 + C2∫dy/z_T² identifies the constant and would-be decaying modes. Duality then supplies analytical estimates of the amplified spectra rather than applying ordinary slow-roll formulae during the non-attractor interval.

sources.title: Gauge Fields and Inflation

evidence.text: Superhorizon end-of-inflation modulation is treated with the δN expansion. Anisotropic perturbations are reduced to physical variables through quadratic actions and evaluated perturbatively using interaction-picture, time-ordered expectation values.

sources.title: Gauge Fields and Inflation

evidence.text: Canonical quantization of gauge modes with transverse polarizations and a time-dependent kinetic function; temporal or Coulomb gauge is used according to the model.

sources.title: Tensor Bounds on the Hidden Universe

evidence.text: Schwinger–Keldysh/in-in perturbation theory uses separately deformed past contours to select the interacting vacuum. Dimensional regularization in 3+δ spatial dimensions includes mode-function, integration-measure and slow-roll corrections, followed by dimension-six counterterms and pivot-scale renormalization.
